clue.text: Soldier given order at start of operation

parts.note: an order or instruction

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: opening letter of operation

explanation.surface: A soldier receives his instructions just as a military operation begins.
explanation.definitionFit: A commando is a soldier trained for raids, a member of an elite assault unit.

clue.text: Cleaner, for example, put up rate

parts.note: a char, or charwoman, is a cleaner

indicators.note: in a down clue, putting something up makes it read from bottom to top

parts.note: e.g. abbreviates for example

explanation.surface: A domestic cleaner, say, has raised her prices.
explanation.walkthrough: A char is an old British term for a woman paid to clean houses.
explanation.definitionFit: A charge is the price asked for something, the same as a rate or fee.

clue.text: Sullen and ill-tempered detective grabbing ring

indicators.note: grabbing something means holding it, so one piece clasps the other

parts.note: Inspector Morse, the Oxford TV detective
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A grumpy detective seizes a ring as evidence.
explanation.walkthrough: Inspector Morse is a famously gloomy British TV detective, which suits the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Morose describes a gloomy, bad-tempered person, matching both sullen and ill-tempered.

clue.text: Legendary beauty devilish man adored

indicators.note: devilish suggests mischief, so the letters are twisted into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A wicked man worshipped a woman of mythical loveliness.
explanation.definitionFit: Andromeda was the Greek princess chained to a rock for her beauty and rescued by Perseus.

clue.text: Helping to support French composer? No second thought required

indicators.note: no second means the abbreviation for a second of time is dropped

parts.note: Léo Delibes, composer of the ballet Coppélia
S is the abbreviation for second
a ration is a helping or portion

explanation.surface: A portion is served to a French composer, without a moment's further consideration.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, the piece that supports another goes beneath it, so the helping comes after the composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Deliberation is careful consideration, a noun synonym of thought.

clue.text: Rise when clubs close

parts.note: as in the sense 'at the time that'
C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs
a close or conclusion

explanation.surface: Something goes up at the moment the nightclubs shut for the night.
explanation.definitionFit: To ascend is to go upward, a straightforward verb synonym for rise.

clue.text: Son, with difficulty, finds a broken piece of pottery

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son
something done hard is done with effort or difficulty

explanation.surface: A boy struggles to locate a fragment of an old pot.
explanation.definitionFit: A shard is a sharp fragment, especially of broken earthenware or glass.

clue.text: Retired American after English warrant

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for English
to warrant is to deserve, to merit
US for American

explanation.surface: A retired American comes after an English legal warrant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' places the American at the end, following English and warrant.
explanation.definitionFit: Emeritus describes a professor or official who has retired but keeps an honorary title.

clue.text: Unproductive results in blind alleys

definitions.meaning: first meaning: lines of enquiry that lead nowhere
second meaning: streets closed at one end

explanation.surface: Fruitless outcomes keep turning up in back streets.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both streets with no exit and, figuratively, courses of action with no prospect of progress.

clue.text: Dog, adult one about to be put on tight lead

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for adult, as in film ratings

indicators.note: tight is slang for drunk, and a drunk word staggers into a new order

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one
re means about or concerning
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A grown dog is to be put on a short leash, held tight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tight lead' reads as a taut leash, but tight means drunk and scrambles the word lead.
explanation.definitionFit: The Airedale is a large terrier breed, so the answer is an example of a dog.

clue.text: Picture producer, one leaving America in disguise

indicators.note: a disguise changes appearance, so the remaining letters are rearranged
something leaving a word departs from it, so those letters are taken out

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one
taken as written

explanation.surface: A film-maker slips out of the USA incognito.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the I from AMERICA and rearrange what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: A camera is the device that takes photographs, so it literally produces pictures.

clue.text: Go-go dancing with Bowie that is encapsulating old style of music

indicators.note: encapsulating means enclosing, so one piece wraps around another
dancing letters move about and land in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
i.e. abbreviates id est, that is
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: David Bowie joins some go-go dancing in a retro musical style.
explanation.walkthrough: The IE wraps around O first, then everything is jumbled together.
explanation.definitionFit: Boogie-woogie is a fast blues piano style with a driving bass, popular in the 1930s and 40s.

clue.text: Rush round with enthusiasm

parts.note: a gust is a sudden rush of wind
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: Someone hurries about eagerly.
explanation.definitionFit: Gusto means hearty relish or zest, a close synonym of enthusiasm.

clue.text: Verbal attack made by bishop on verge

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
the verge is the grassy edge of a road, the roadside

explanation.surface: A cleric launches a tirade while standing at the side of the road.
explanation.walkthrough: A verge, in British usage, is the strip of grass beside a road.
explanation.definitionFit: A broadside, originally a ship's full volley of guns, is figuratively a fierce spoken or written attack.

clue.text: Ride, a bit drunk, on bypass

parts.note: merry means tipsy
to go round something is to bypass it

explanation.surface: A tipsy person takes a ride along the bypass road.
explanation.definitionFit: A merry-go-round is a fairground carousel, a ride with revolving wooden horses.

clue.text: The origin of a problem, so acute or otherwise

indicators.note: otherwise means in a different way, so the letters are arranged differently

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Where a difficulty starts, whether it is severe or not.
explanation.definitionFit: The root cause is the fundamental underlying reason something has gone wrong.

clue.text: Professional shot wide, we hear, and swore

parts.note: pro is short for professional

indicators.note: we hear points to a word recognised by its sound rather than its spelling

parts.note: a shot that goes wide has missed

explanation.surface: A golf pro sliced his drive and cursed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swore' looks like cursing, but it is the sense of making a solemn vow.
explanation.definitionFit: To have promised and to have sworn both mean to have given a solemn pledge.

clue.text: Golfing group, perhaps in favour of fee, by the sound of it

indicators.note: the sound of words matters here rather than their spelling

parts.note: for means in favour of
a fee is a sum of money

explanation.surface: Some golfers seem to support charging a fee.
explanation.definitionFit: A foursome is a group of four, typically a golf match of two pairs, so 'perhaps' marks it as one example.

clue.text: Novel metaphor Otto translated

indicators.note: translating changes the form of words, so these letters are recast in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man named Otto renders a figure of speech in a work of fiction into another language.
explanation.definitionFit: Room at the Top is John Braine's 1957 novel about an ambitious young man, so it is an example of a novel.

clue.text: Three consecutive letters from a spiritual leader?

definitions.text: Three consecutive letters from a spiritual leader?

parts.words: Three consecutive letters from a spiritual leader?
parts.note: surface reading: three letters in a row written by some guru
setter's reading: the alphabet letters that follow F, written out as the seventh, then the word 'and', then the next two together

explanation.walkthrough: The answer splits as G AND HI, three alphabetically consecutive letters joined by 'and'; the question mark flags the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Mahatma Gandhi led India's independence movement and is revered as a spiritual and moral leader.

clue.text: Whole convent I renovated? Just a part

indicators.note: only a part of the following words is needed, a run of letters inside them

parts.note: the letters run across the three words

explanation.surface: Was the whole nunnery refurbished, or only one section?
explanation.definitionFit: Entire and whole both mean complete, with nothing missing.

clue.text: Old lady, right to attend county game with traveller

parts.note: one's old lady is one's mother, ma
R is the abbreviation for right
Co. is the abbreviation for county
polo is a game played on horseback

explanation.surface: An elderly woman rightly goes to watch a county match with someone on a journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To attend' places the right just before the county.
explanation.definitionFit: Marco Polo was the Venetian merchant famed for his journey to China, the archetypal traveller.

clue.text: Hatred coming from platform lacking leadership

indicators.note: with no leader, the word loses its opening letter

parts.note: a podium is a raised platform

explanation.surface: Hostility is voiced from a stage by someone with no leader.
explanation.definitionFit: Odium is general loathing or disgust directed at someone, a formal word for hatred.

clue.text: Measure mountain range

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an old unit of length, 22 yards
second meaning: a connected line of peaks

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as an instruction to gauge some mountains, but the two parts define separately.
explanation.definitionFit: A chain is an imperial length of 22 yards, and also a series of linked mountains.

clue.text: Unemotional, head of technology in firm

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the other here

parts.note: firm and solid are synonyms

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: first letter of technology

explanation.surface: A dispassionate tech chief working in a company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Firm' looks like a company, but it is the adjective meaning solid.
explanation.definitionFit: A stolid person is impassive and shows little feeling, hence unemotional.

clue.text: Emblem of Christ, possibly 500 guineas

indicators.note: possibly hints these letters could be arranged otherwise

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500
taken as written

explanation.surface: A religious symbol might cost five hundred guineas.
explanation.walkthrough: A guinea is an old British gold coin worth 21 shillings.
explanation.definitionFit: Agnus Dei, Latin for Lamb of God, is the lamb image used as a symbol of Christ.

clue.text: Read my novel, it's wonderful

indicators.note: novel means new, so these letters take a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An author urges you to read their book, boasting how great it is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like a book; it is an adjective signalling new order.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, dreamy means delightful or lovely, as in a dreamy holiday.

clue.text: Beer brewed by agreeable girl

indicators.note: brewing mixes and transforms ingredients, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
nice means pleasant or agreeable

explanation.surface: A pleasant young woman has made some home-brewed ale.
explanation.definitionFit: Berenice is a female first name, so it stands as an example of a girl.
